evidence: The codebase is organized into logical, cohesive modules (e.g., mmseg.datasets, mmseg.models, mmseg.apis, mmseg.core) with clear separation of concerns but no inter-service communication protocols.

Repository structure shows hierarchical module organization: models/backbones, models/decode_heads, models/necks, models/segmentors, etc., indicating strong internal cohesion and dependency-driven modularity—not loose coupling typical of microservices.
Total package count is 20, avg_fan_out is low (~1.1), and max_directory_depth is 5, consistent with a well-structured single deployment unit.
All components are imported directly via Python modules (e.g., from mmseg.models import build_segmentor), with no service calls, message queues, REST/gRPC interfaces, or deployment isolation.
Training/inference uses local function calls (e.g., train_segmentor, inference_segmentor) within the same process—no network boundaries.
Build/test/deployment tooling (tools/train.py, tools/test.py, setup.py, tests) treats the system as a single deployable unit—no orchestration or service discovery.
Registry pattern (mmcv.utils.Registry + build_from_cfg) used extensively across modules, indicating design for extensibility within a unified codebase, not service interaction.
risks: Limited scalability—vertical scaling only due to monolithic execution.
Higher risk of tight coupling if modularity boundaries are violated (though current structure shows good discipline).
Harder to deploy heterogeneous technologies for different workloads (e.g., inference vs training).
